title: Correct altitude value
description: Essential Criteria: The final numerical answer for the mountain's altitude must be 6000 m (or 6 km).

title: Gravitational acceleration relationship
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly relate gravitational acceleration at sea level (g) and at height H (g_H) using Newton's law of universal gravitation (g ∝ 1/R²).

title: Pendulum period relationship
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly apply the formula for the period of a simple pendulum (T = 2π√(L/g)) to relate periods at the two locations.

title: Oscillation count and total time
description: Important Criteria: The solution must establish that the same total time interval is given by 500*T = 501*T_0, linking the number of oscillations to the periods.

title: Algebraic simplification to ratio
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should correctly simplify the equations to obtain the clean ratio g/g_H = (501/500)² or its equivalent.

title: Unit consistency and conversion
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should demonstrate consistent unit handling, particularly converting the planet's radius from kilometers to meters if needed for the final answer.

title: Incorrect period-oscillation relationship
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student inverts the relationship between oscillation count and period (e.g., assumes 500 oscillations correspond to the shorter period).

title: Sign or exponent error in gravity
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize errors in the gravitational acceleration formula, such as using (R+H) instead of (R+H)² in the denominator, or misplacing the square.
